A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPIN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the image-based qualitative examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination evaluations, attention analyses, ablations, throughput measurements, and qualitative examples for SPIN.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds MME/MMMU evaluations, newer-model experiments, and a VTI comparison.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same per-token image-attention ranking, top-k head selection, suppression factor, and three-stage hyperparameter selection. The background attention-equation correction does not establish a change to SPIN's implemented procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MME and MMMU evaluations, extending coverage beyond hallucination-focused captioning and VQA to general perception, cognition, and multidisciplinary multimodal reasoning. The existing COCO-based and OpenImages-based coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds VTI to the LLaVA-1.5 (7B) greedy CHAIR comparison. Existing comparators remain in their corresponding experiments. ICT is newly discussed in related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLaVA-Next (7B) and Qwen2.5-VL (7B) configurations and specifies full-MME and MMMU-validation evaluation, including weighted overall MMMU scoring and reuse of CHAIR suppression settings. Existing CHAIR/POPE sample sizes and decoding protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's Appendix A.5 and Figure 8, containing two POPE case studies for random and adversarial questions, are removed. The suppression, layer-selection, head-selection, and repetition analyses, head-mask visualization, and CHAIR case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its results. The added evaluations continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Tables 5, 6, 12, and 13, plus VTI's Table 1 row; existing quantitative results remain unchanged. New comparisons include MMMU overall scores of 36.6 versus 36.9 for baseline/SPIN LLaVA-1.5 (13B), and MME cognition scores of 590.7 versus 552.5 for Qwen2.5-VL. Two POPE qualitative examples are removed.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the attention-scaling denominator from sqrt(d_k/H) to sqrt(d_k), with d_k = d/H retained. This changes the mathematical expression, rather than merely its notation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: dynamic image-inattentive head suppression, inference-only operation with negligible overhead, up to 2.7-fold hallucination reduction, and up to 1.8-fold throughput improvement.

C2.justification: v2 attributes pruning-related F1 losses to unadapted pretrained weights and explains Qwen2.5-VL's lower suppression ratio through greater responsibility per head. Section 4.6 newly interprets general-capability results as preservation or enhancement, while acknowledging a cognition decline for Qwen2.5-VL. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that MMHal-Bench and GPT-4o evaluations reuse CHAIR suppression settings. Tables 12 and 13 disclose configurations for the added models, and Appendix A.5 specifies their backbone, layer, and head information. Existing hardware, baseline hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds VTI and ICT, positioning SPIN against steering-vector and classifier-guided activation interventions. References for MME, MMMU, LLaVA-Next, and Qwen2.5-VL are also added. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing standardizes model names and top-k notation, corrects affiliation text, and expands several explanations. A general-performance subsection is inserted, and Appendix A.5 changes from POPE visualization to newer-model evaluation. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four result tables, a VTI row, and explicit Baseline/SPIN labels in the retained appendix POPE table. It removes the POPE example figure and resizes the retained CHAIR panels to text width. Existing plots remain unchanged, with localized relocation, caption editing, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added general-capability and newer-model evaluations better document applicability and tradeoffs, while the corrected attention equation and parameter disclosures improve technical clarity. The gain is limited by overbroad capability-enhancement language despite mixed MME results, particularly Qwen2.5-VL's cognition decline in Table 5, and absent uncertainty estimates for small MMMU differences.
